chunks: Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb narrated from Sayf ibn ʿUmīrah, from Ibn Muskān, from Ibrāhīm ibn Shuʿayb who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him): 'Verily my father has become very old and weak, so we carry him when he needs to relieve himself.' He said: 'If you can continue doing that [yourself] then do so, and feed him morsels with your own hand, for that will be a shield for you tomorrow [from the Fire].'

key_terms.تَلِىَ: To continue doing or persist in an action

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for physically caring for an elderly parent according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Zuhd*, Imam al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him) elevates physical service to a frail father to the level of spiritual protection, specifically highlighting the act of feeding him by hand as a 'Garden' (Jannah) for the next day. This emphasizes the Shia scholarly view that tangible, humble acts of care for aging parents serve as a direct intercessory shield against the Hellfire, reinforcing the concept of *birr al-wālidayn* (kindness to parents) as a practical path to salvation.
